partnershipPlan: A maternity voices group, including women who needed an interpreter, reviews the information leaflet, the paper diary and the hub call script before recruitment.
socialListening: No social media listening; the unit's postnatal feedback comments from the last year are read for mentions of blood pressure checks.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: Twice a day sounds easy until you are feeding every two hours and the cuff is somewhere under the baby blanket.
items.implication: Allow a flexible reading window and report the burden outcome.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: When the midwife rang after a high reading I felt someone was watching over me, not that I was in trouble.
items.implication: Keep hub calls warm and prompt.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase (through an interpreter): My phone only makes calls; I thought the monitoring was not for women like me.
items.implication: Offer paper diaries and hub calls in the woman's language.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase (assessment unit midwife): The worst readings come at night, when the hub is closed.

summary: Four composite voices on burden, reassurance, digital access and night-time readings.
